description: Read-only, reproducible simulation fixture for the P-002.6 dependency-aware wave scheduler. Verification parses shipment 130-S itself, filters its task-type IDs into M, parses the live status catalog and registry mapping/features, exact-compares M with the explicit non-shipment fallback task-ID set, reports excluded non-task IDs, and projects task contracts from the live backlog; scenarios and expectations encode the cycle-34 corrected contract. Executed by scripts/wave-scheduler-sim.ps1; no repository state is mutated.

source.note: Run scripts/wave-scheduler-sim.ps1 -VerifyAgainstQueue to parse the real shipment item list, live status catalog, and registry status mapping/features; resolve artifact types; compare filtered task IDs exactly with M and the explicit non-shipment fallback set; report excluded non-task IDs; verify task projections and every red-deliverable key; and run in-memory mutation checks.

status_model.note: The scheduler vocabulary and source-selection features are CONFIGURED, never hard-coded. -VerifyAgainstQueue parses and compares the ten-token workspace catalog, the four-entry registry status mapping, and the sql_query/shipments feature flags live. Terminal-success is the two-token actual lifecycle {done, archived}. Every catalog token outside executable + terminal_success is unsupported and halts. archived satisfies a DEPENDENCY but does NOT close a green-maker obligation, because it may be a descope.

manifest.note: S is all 44 explicit members of shipment 130-S. M is exactly the 43 IDs in S whose resolved artifact_type is task. The explicit non-shipment fallback is the same closed 43-ID set, supplied rather than inferred from parent children. The covering feature 147-F and retired archived sibling 147.010-T are forbidden wave IDs: neither is in M, the fallback, or a snapshot.

red_deliverables.red_deliverable_reason: Harness-only behaviour contract for the guarded rewrite seam; the seam's implementation is 147.036-T / U13, so this task's three TestU12_ functions are red by design when it completes.

Verb-level conformance refusal harness that must be observed red before the seam migration; the refusal is delivered by 147.037-T / U14, so this task's single TestU3c_ function is red by design when it completes.

Cross-surface parity harness with no production change; its assertions turn green only after every surface implementation it pins has landed, so its TestU8b_ functions are red by design when it completes.

green_regression_parser_controls.error_contains: payload must be a JSON object

red_deliverable_branch_controls.note: The deliverable: the scaffolded harness compiles, the anchored selector fails on named assertions, the delta is empty, and the evidence report is complete.
Routing: an ordinary dispatch still enters the generic loop, so Step 0.5 does not capture tasks it does not own.
Load-bearing control: the same green observation the generic loop reads as SUCCESS must halt here instead.
Step 0.5a: the scaffolded selector already passes before any declared green-maker has closed.
Step 0.5a: no test matches the declared selector, so the harness was never scaffolded under it and the red is vacuous.
Step 0.5a item 1: a harness that does not compile contradicts the P-002 compiling-but-failing contract and returns to harness-architect.
Step 0.5a: a panic aborts the package with no matching --- FAIL: line, so it is not the deliverable.
Step 0.5a: a timeout is a non-zero exit that proves no assertion failed.
Step 0.5b: the branch writes nothing, and a non-test *.go file is the production change a red deliverable may never make.
Step 0.5b: a *_test.go file is still a write; the permitted delta is empty, so a test extension is not an exemption.
Step 0.5b: a configuration or documentation file is a write too.
Precondition 3 fails closed: without the Ship-supplied post-scaffolding baseline the zero-delta gate would measure a self-chosen range.
Precondition 1: red_deliverable and harness-exempt are mutually exclusive.
Precondition 2: harness_cmd must be the declared red_selector_command verbatim.
Precondition 2: a bare ./... with no -count=1, no anchored selector, and a || true suffix is a contract defect, not a substitute command.
Step 0.5c: without the report Ship cannot build the open_red_deliverables entry that convergence items 4 and 5 re-confirm.
Step 0.5b: a newly created *_test.go file is invisible to git diff, so the gate must include the untracked pass or an empty-delta claim would be false.
Step 0.5b: a newly created non-test *.go file is still the production change a red deliverable may never make.

scenarios.description: Unmutated manifest replays the documented 18-wave schedule with no stall and no compile-order violation. snapshot_calls is 19 = one per build wave plus the final admission snapshot that observes terminal_success = M.

Red-deliverable selectors stay open across waves; wave 4 advances while U8b and U3c are legitimately red; every entry still open after a wave's completions - including entries carried in from an earlier wave - has its red_selector_command re-run and re-confirmed RED at that wave's convergence gate; the unfiltered full suite runs only when the open-red set is empty, and immediately at the wave where the last green-maker closes it.
A blocked member halts the loop at the first admission that sees it, reports transitive dependency impact, stays in M, and never permits a completion claim.
A member blocked mid-run halts at the next wave admission rather than being skipped.
An active leftover claim halts with WAVE_NO_PROGRESS rather than being read as progress.
A catalog token that is neither executable nor terminal-success halts with WAVE_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED naming the member and the observed token.
A non-completion terminal token never false-completes: abandoned is unsupported, not terminal-success.
A token outside the workspace catalog entirely is unsupported and halts; it is never treated as an implicit success.
An unreadable or empty configured status catalog halts before any admission; the scheduler never falls back to a built-in token list.
A configured executable or terminal-success token absent from the workspace catalog is a disagreement, not a widening; it halts.
A dependency cycle halts at Step 3 schedule construction with the cycle path, never at runtime and never by looping.

Wave 4 has five simultaneously-red non-exempt members. The withdrawn repo-wide per-task gate progresses none of them; the task-scoped gate progresses all five, and no full suite runs inside a per-task loop.
Negative control: re-deriving M from the live shipment items list each wave lets return_blocked shrink the accounting universe. The frozen-M contract exists to prevent exactly this.
A red-deliverable task whose green-maker mapping is absent fails closed at schedule construction; the mapping is never inferred.
A green-maker naming a task outside M is ambiguous and fails closed; it is never resolved by nearest match.
An empty red_selector_command fails closed at schedule construction; selector scope is never inferred from the task title, unit, or package.
A green_maker_closes_wave value that does not equal the actual latest green-maker wave fails closed at schedule construction.

A green-maker archived (descoped) rather than done satisfies dependencies but does NOT close its open-red obligation; the deferral budget then halts the loop instead of carrying an unverifiable red forward.

Negative control for the convergence gate's open-red re-confirmation. 147.042-T / U3c completes red in wave 4 and its declared green-maker 147.037-T / U14 does not land until wave 8. Its selector is injected green from wave 5 - three waves early. Because the gate re-runs the red_selector_command of every entry still open after the wave's completions, including entries carried in from an earlier wave, the violation is caught at the wave-5 gate and the loop halts with WAVE_RED_DELIVERABLE_EARLY_GREEN instead of advancing. Without that always-run item the entry would never be executed again while the unfiltered suite stayed deferred, and the early green would pass unnoticed through waves 5 to 8.

Complement of the control above: an entry the wave CLOSED is not re-confirmed RED - it is re-confirmed GREEN instead. 147.035-T / U12 is closed by 147.036-T / U13 at wave 7, and its selector is injected green from wave 7. Because a closed entry leaves the open set before the RED re-confirmation and enters newly_closed_k instead, the injection is the expected outcome rather than a violation and the schedule completes - proving the gate re-confirms RED over exactly the still-open set and no more.

Negative control for the newly-closed verification. 147.036-T / U13 is 147.035-T / U12's only declared green-maker and completes in wave 7, so U12 leaves the open set at the wave-7 gate. Its selector is injected as still failing. Because 147.016-T / U8b keeps the open-red set non-empty until wave 13, the unfiltered full suite stays deferred and would not surface the failure until six waves later - so the gate must verify newly closed selectors itself. It halts at wave 7 with WAVE_GREEN_MAKER_UNVERIFIED rather than advancing on an unverified green-maker.
